alt.en: A detail of an old printed column. A paragraph beginning "We now come to the hauling shanties" explains that when many men pull on one rope, the pull is made at a particular word in the chorus. Below are two short verses, the second reading "Haul the bowline, the fore and main-top bowline, Haul the bowline, the bowline haul; Haul the bowline, Kitty you're my darling, Haul the bowline, the bowline haul." The last line reads "Here the concluding word of each couplet, haul, gives the clue".
alt.es: Detalle de una columna impresa antigua. Un párrafo que empieza "We now come to the hauling shanties" explica que, cuando muchos hombres tiran de un mismo cabo, el tirón se da en una palabra concreta del estribillo. Debajo hay dos estrofas cortas; la segunda dice "Haul the bowline, the fore and main-top bowline, Haul the bowline, the bowline haul; Haul the bowline, Kitty you're my darling, Haul the bowline, the bowline haul." La última línea dice "Here the concluding word of each couplet, haul, gives the clue".

caption.en: "On Shanties" in the London weekly Once a Week, 1 August 1868, page 93: the earliest printing of the chorus we found, with the writer's note that the last word, "haul", is the clue for the pull.
caption.es: "On Shanties" en el semanario londinense Once a Week, 1 de agosto de 1868, página 93: la impresión más antigua del estribillo que hemos encontrado, con la nota del autor de que la última palabra, "haul", es la señal para tirar.

source: "On Shanties" (unsigned), Once a Week, new series, no. 31 (London: Bradbury, Evans & Co., 1 August 1868), p. 93, detail of the left column (from "We now come to the hauling shanties" to "gives the clue; there are many of this sort")

alt.en: A detail of an old printed magazine column. The text reads ""Bowline," one of the purest of generic pulling songs:". Below are two short lines of music in 4/4. The first, marked "Solo. Moderato.", has the words "We'll haul the bowline so early in the morning." The second, marked "Chorus.", has the words "We'll haul the bow-line, the bow-line haul!"
alt.es: Detalle de una columna impresa de una revista antigua. El texto dice ""Bowline," one of the purest of generic pulling songs:". Debajo hay dos líneas cortas de música en 4/4. La primera, marcada "Solo. Moderato.", lleva las palabras "We'll haul the bowline so early in the morning." La segunda, marcada "Chorus.", lleva las palabras "We'll haul the bow-line, the bow-line haul!"

caption.en: William L. Alden's "Bowline" in Harper's New Monthly Magazine, New York, July 1882, page 282: the earliest tune for the song we found, with the shantyman's line "We'll haul the bowline so early in the morning".
caption.es: El "Bowline" de William L. Alden en Harper's New Monthly Magazine, Nueva York, julio de 1882, página 282: la melodía más antigua de la canción que hemos encontrado, con el verso del solista "We'll haul the bowline so early in the morning".

alt.en: A printed page of music, page 42, headed "XXXVII. Haul on the Bow-line.", with four systems, each a voice part above a two-stave piano part, in 4/4. The voice part is marked "Solo. (Introduction.)", then "Solo." and "Chorus." in turn, with the words "Haul on the bow-line, O Kit-ty you are my dar-ling" and "Be-cause she had a fore-top, fore and main to bow-line" under the notes. A small arrowhead stands over the word "haul" at the end of each chorus.
alt.es: Página impresa de música, página 42, con el encabezado "XXXVII. Haul on the Bow-line.", con cuatro sistemas, cada uno con una voz sobre un acompañamiento de piano en dos pentagramas, en 4/4. La voz está marcada "Solo. (Introduction.)" y luego, alternando, "Solo." y "Chorus.", con las palabras "Haul on the bow-line, O Kit-ty you are my dar-ling" y "Be-cause she had a fore-top, fore and main to bow-line" bajo las notas. Una pequeña punta de flecha está sobre la palabra "haul" al final de cada estribillo.

caption.en: Haul on the Bow-line as No. XXXVII of Cecil Sharp's English Folk-Chanteys (London, 1914), as John Short of Watchet sang it: our arrangement is read from this page, and the arrowhead over each chorus's last "haul" marks the pull.
caption.es: Haul on the Bow-line como n.º XXXVII de English Folk-Chanteys de Cecil Sharp (Londres, 1914), tal como la cantaba John Short, de Watchet: nuestro arreglo se lee en esta página, y la punta de flecha sobre el último "haul" de cada estribillo marca el tirón.

alt.en: An old black-and-white photograph printed in a book. On the deck of a sailing ship at sea, a line of men in work clothes and caps bend forward and pull together on a rope; at the left, two men reach up to a rope beside the mast. A large sail fills the top of the picture, a coil of rope lies on the deck and the sea shows beyond the rail. Below it is printed "Blow, my bully boys, blow".
alt.es: Fotografía antigua en blanco y negro impresa en un libro. En la cubierta de un velero en alta mar, una fila de hombres con ropa de trabajo y gorras se inclinan hacia delante y tiran a la vez de un cabo; a la izquierda, dos hombres levantan los brazos hacia un cabo junto al palo. Una gran vela ocupa la parte de arriba de la imagen, hay un rollo de cabo en la cubierta y se ve el mar más allá de la borda. Debajo está impreso "Blow, my bully boys, blow".

caption.en: A crew hauling together at sea, from a photograph by Paul Eve Stevenson in By Way of Cape Horn (Philadelphia, 1899), his account of a voyage in a Yankee sailing ship, printed under a shanty line he named among the best for hauling.
caption.es: Una tripulación halando a la vez en alta mar, en una fotografía de Paul Eve Stevenson publicada en By Way of Cape Horn (Filadelfia, 1899), su relato de un viaje en un velero estadounidense, bajo un verso de shanty que él contaba entre los mejores para halar.

source: Paul Eve Stevenson, By Way of Cape Horn: Four Months in a Yankee Clipper, "illustrated from photographs taken by the author" (Philadelphia: J. B. Lippincott Company, 1899), plate facing p. 104, "Blow, my bully boys, blow"
